REAL ESTATE

30-Year Fixed: 7.27% unchanged  |  15-Year Fixed: 6.92% unchanged

The housing market just flipped, nationally. Redfin says the typical U.S. home sold for $389,601 in the four weeks to Oct. 25, down 0.1% from a year earlier, the first annual decline in more than three years. Apartment List says the national median rent, $1,384, is now 0.1% above a year ago, its first annual gain in over three years.

Here it flipped at least a year ago. Zillow's September data has rents up in all five of our cities, from 3.9% in Hayward to 10.1% in Milpitas, and typical home values down in all five, from 1.2% in Milpitas to 2.4% in Hayward and Newark. A year earlier, values were falling 3% to 7% and rents rising 1% to 3.5%, so the declines are shrinking while rent gains speed up. Next door, Redfin has San Jose sale prices down 4.9% and San Francisco's up 15%.

Rates held. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.27% and the 15-year 6.92%, unchanged since Friday. At 7.27%, a Fremont buyer at today's $1,329,000 median with 20% down would pay about $7,267 a month in principal and interest, about 2.1 times Zillow's $3,388 typical Fremont rent. The gap is still wide, but it is closing from both ends.

What it means for you. If you rent, your next renewal notice is a good reason to price a purchase while values sit below last year; 272 of the 575 homes on the market in our five cities are priced under a million. If you are selling, buyers can see these numbers too, and 180 homes have been sitting 60 days or longer, so price to this year's market, not last year's.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,457 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,482, with 155 coming soon and 139 brand new. The five city ledger carries 648 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 575 on the market and 73 coming soon, down from 650. Coming soon rose to 73 from 67, so more supply is on deck.

Fremont holds 221 live listings: 165 active, 34 coming soon, 21 brand new and 1 back on the market, with a median on market list price of $1,329,000 at $825 a square foot and a typical listing out 36 days. Hayward carries 183, Milpitas 99 and Newark 84, all unchanged, and Union City 61 (from 64). Across all five cities the median is $1,075,000 at $668 a square foot, 272 homes are priced under a million, and 180 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

STOCKS

S&P 500: 7,541.40 -0.51%  |  Dow: 51,983.98 +0.41%  |  Nasdaq: 25,164.31 -1.07%

Tech is bouncing. The numbers above are Monday's closes, when the Nasdaq fell 1.07% to its lowest close since July 30 while the Dow gained 0.41%. As of 8:00 AM PT Tuesday the Nasdaq is up 1.03%, the S&P 500 up 0.58% and the Dow down 0.20%.

Two strong quarters, two lower stocks. Apple posted record September quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12%, with iPhone sales up 17% to $57.6 billion; the stock is down 2.7%. Palantir's revenue rose 96% to $2.31 billion, and its U.S. commercial sales passed its government sales for the first time; its shares are down 1.5%. A great quarter is not the same as a surprise.

ECONOMY

10-Year Treasury: 4.91% -0.03  |  Gold: $3,969.60 +1.81%  |  Silver: $50.89 +3.27%  |  Brent Crude: $104.77 -7.63%

Oil's slide held. Brent settled Monday at $104.77, down 7.6%, after Iran signaled talks that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and it is down another 1.59% this morning. Cheaper oil would help with inflation, which ran 3.7% in September with core at 2.6%. With inflation there, two Fed officials voted for a rate hike last week, and mortgage rates are still above 7%.

Metals bounced. Gold rose 1.81% Monday to $3,969.60 and silver 3.27% to $50.89 after Friday's selloff, and both are giving some back this morning. The numbers above are Monday's settlements and Treasury's close; Brent is the January contract, measured against January's $113.43 Friday settlement.

CRYPTOCURRENCY

Bitcoin: $77,635 +0.28%  |  Ethereum: $2,297.86 +1.17%  |  XRP: $1.28 +2.53%

Users rushed out of Binance. Binance reopened withdrawals Sunday after last week's record $6.3 billion hack, and in the first 9.5 hours customers pulled out $4.65 billion and put in $1.01 billion, a $3.64 billion net outflow. That was 2.1% of its $171 billion in assets, and Binance says it has covered about 95% of the stolen amount, up from 90%.

Bitcoin took it calmly. It is up 0.28% over 24 hours, Ether up 1.17% and XRP up 2.53%, live from CoinGecko at 8:00 AM PT. Covered is not recovered: Binance is shouldering the loss itself, though Circle says it has frozen more than $1.1 billion in USDC tied to the theft.
